claims.text: The initial FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy is single-phase fcc.
Aging at 500°C for 2 hours will precipitate Co-rich nanoparticles in the FeCoNi-based alloy.
The precipitated Co-rich nanoparticles constitute a secondary phase.
Co-rich nanoparticles will pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning by Co-rich nanoparticles will reduce magnetic domain size.
Domain-wall pinning will increase the coercive field.
Introducing precipitated Co-rich nanoparticles will overcome the coercivity limitation of single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The modified alloy will have a coercive field at least 50% higher than single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The baseline coercive field is 100 Oe.
The modified alloy will have a coercive field of 150 Oe.
The proposed effect applies within FeCoNi-based alloys having an fcc matrix and potential secondary phases.
The size and distribution of Co-rich nanoparticles and their domain-wall-pinning effect are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 50% increase from 100 Oe to 150 Oe, whereas the falsification rule treats any result above 100 Oe as sufficient to avoid falsification. For example, 110 Oe would pass the stated falsification threshold while failing the stated predicted increase.
